description: Figure 6(a) is a bar chart that illustrates the distribution of datasets over time, categorized by the number of languages in which they are published. The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning from 2012 to 2022. The vertical axis, labeled "Number of datasets," is on a logarithmic scale, with values ranging from $10^0$ (1 dataset) to $10^2$ (100 datasets). The chart displays two sets of bars for each year: blue bars represent datasets in a single language ("1"), and orange bars represent datasets in two or more languages ("2+"). The data shows a general increase in the number of datasets over time. The number of monolingual datasets (blue bars) is consistently higher than the number of multilingual datasets (orange bars) in most years. A notable shift occurs around 2017, where the number of multilingual datasets begins to rise significantly, surpassing the number of monolingual datasets in 2021 and 2022. The caption indicates that this figure compares the five most frequent researcher locations with all other locations combined, and that researchers from the US publish the most consistently.
